full_text: 01 · OPPORTUNITY The problem 02 Today’s AI answers very well. But answering is not the same as teaching. “Explain percentages” Does not know the real level Does not remember what worked Confuses an answer with mastery To teach, AI needs… Diagnosis Know where the learner starts. Path Define what to learn and in what order. Memory Remember evidence, not only messages. Proof Demonstrate understanding and transfer. Answering ≠ teaching 2

texts: The difference is not better conversation. It is how learning is decided, remembered, and proven.

Educational chatbot Multi-agent tutor Open conversation Measurable goals Chat memory Profile + graph + evidence One explanation Multiple strategies & hints Right / wrong Rubrics + reasoning Optional sources Research + verify + curate Moves on by request Moves on by mastery TEACHING IS A SYSTEM, NOT A PROMPT 6

texts: Instead of memorizing 12 agent names, think of four teams with separate responsibilities.
Understand the goal and build the path
Assess and fix the root cause

full_text: 06 · GOVERNANCE Twelve specialists, one tutor 07 Instead of memorizing 12 agent names, think of four teams with separate responsibilities. 1 · COORDINATE Understand the goal and build the path Orchestrator Profile & diagnosis Planner 2 · TEACH Explain, connect, and practice Tutor Connections Generator 3 · MEASURE Assess and fix the root cause Evaluator Remediation Researcher 4 · PROTECT Govern sources, truth, and safety Curator Verifier Safety Separation of duties prevents the system from “approving itself.” 7

texts: The tutor connects new knowledge to something the learner already understands.
The tutor checks whether the bridge worked

What is already mastered Analogy / example New concept The tutor checks whether the bridge worked Reuses previous examples Marks where the analogy stops Remembers which connections work More use → better teaching 8

texts: Research, verification, and curation are different jobs. Separating them reduces hallucinations.
Decide what is included, updated, or removed.
Sensitive topics → safety can block or escalate to human review.
full_text: 09 · TRUST Trust: sources are not improvised 10 Research, verification, and curation are different jobs. Separating them reduces hallucinations. 1 Research Find candidate resources. 2 Verify Check citations, contradictions, and confidence. 3 Curate Decide what is included, updated, or removed. Sensitive topics → safety can block or escalate to human review. 10

texts: Pedagogy is the core. Models and databases can change without rebuilding the product.

PEDAGOGICAL CORE AI models Replaceable Orchestration Python · LangChain · LangGraph Data PostgreSQL · Neo4j · Vector DB Adapters SQL / Cypher / APIs Changing providers ≠ rewriting how the system teaches 11

texts: Start with goal-driven learners. Expand to teachers, institutions, and companies.

full_text: 11 · INITIAL MARKET Who we serve 12 Start with goal-driven learners. Expand to teachers, institutions, and companies. Self-learners Learn a skill with a clear path. Professionals Upgrade skills with evidence. Teachers Extend instruction and follow-up. Companies Train for competence, not attendance. MVP: Spanish + a few tightly scoped domains → depth before breadth. 12

texts: The MVP must prove one thing: evidence of learning.
Connects to mastered ratios and creates a short practice task.
full_text: 12 · DEMO The minimum viable product 13 The MVP must prove one thing: evidence of learning. 1 · DIAGNOSIS Goal: learn percentages ✓ Masters ratios △ Unsure with fractions → Personalized path 2 · LESSON “50% means half” Connects to mastered ratios and creates a short practice task. Previously successful example 3 · EVIDENCE Result 83% mastery 1 gap detected Remediation triggered Success = evidence of learning 13

texts: We do not promise magic. We design how failures are detected, contained, and escalated.
Verify sources; cite or stay silent.
Models matched to complexity and budget.
We design how the system fails, not only how it works.
full_text: 15 · RISK & CONTROL Risks designed from day one 16 We do not promise magic. We design how failures are detected, contained, and escalated. Hallucinations Verify sources; cite or stay silent. Unfair assessment Rubrics + multiple evidence + human review. Token costs Models matched to complexity and budget. Vendor lock-in Replaceable ports and adapters. Privacy Consent, isolation, and deletion. Multi-agent complexity Clear contracts + one orchestrator. We design how the system fails, not only how it works. 16

texts: Short answers to the questions investors are most likely to ask.
Teaching, grading, searching, and verifying have different incentives.
What if the AI provider changes?
Pedagogy is separated from the model; the adapter can be replaced.
How do we know learning happened?
Concept mastery, retention, transfer, and resolved gaps.
The architecture allows it, but launch requires age, consent, and stronger safeguards.
How long does the MVP take?
It depends on domain and team; scope is already limited to the full learning loop.
Still to be chosen: professional skills, coding, languages, or internal training.
